recipes.name: Fresh Strawberry Upside-Down Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 (6 ounce) package strawberry flavored Jell-O® mix
1 (18 ounce) package yellow cake mix, batter prepared as directed on package

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Spread crushed strawberries on the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish; sprinkle gelatin powder over strawberries, then top with mini marshmallows.
Combine cake mix, water, eggs, and oil in a large bowl; beat with an electric mixer on low speed until moistened. Increase speed to medium and beat for 2 minutes. Pour batter on top of marshmallows.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, 40 to 50 minutes.
Cool cake in the pan for 15 minutes. Run a knife around edges, then turn out the cake onto a serving plate, strawberry side up. Store cake in the refrigerator.

raw_recipe.headline: Fresh Strawberry Upside-Down Cake
raw_recipe.description: This upside-down strawberry cake is so easy to make with boxed cake mix, strawberries, strawberry gelatin, and marshmallows for a fab summer dessert.

review.reviewBody: I've made this twice and discovered two very important parts of the recipe that you can *not* overlook: 1) Use fresh strawberries or your own frozen. Commercially frozen doesn't interact as well with the Jello for some reason. 2) MASH the strawberries. The juice has to be released or there's nothing to break down the gelatin and you get a very unpleasant texture on the top of your cake. If your strawberries aren't very juicy, sprinkle a little sugar on them before mashing and let them set for an hour or so - the juice will come out. The cake by itself is pretty, but it does need whipped cream or ice cream (heat the cake up slightly) to finish it off for eating.

OK, first of all. OMG, this cake was SO good. I just got done making it, not only is it freakin' gorgeous as it is fresh out of the oven, it -tastes- amazing. It's moist and delicious. The jello trickling throughout the cake was awesome. I'm totally in love with this recipe. It's incredibly simple too! I made a few changes ONLY and only because I really wanted to try this and didn't have exactly what you called for. I replaced your strawberries with frozen (thawed) strawberry slices I had on hand. I also didn't have strawberry jello, I used what I did have; Raspberry. I love how this cake has marshmallows in it. I wasn't sure how that was going to turn out but as it is, it adds crunch when you're not expecting it. Sooooo yummy. This cake was again, super easy to make and loads of fun. Each step from placing the strawberries to pouring the cake batter was neat. I smiled the whole time in excitement to try this cake. I just had the first piece and I give you 5 stars. :) Thank you for sharing this with the world.

Changes I made are due to being a diabetic. I used a sugar free yellow cake mix and added 1 small box of sugar free instant pudding powder. I also substituted the 1 cup of water with pineapple juice from large can of crushed pineapple.
I diced half of the strawberries in a bowl and stirred in 3oz of sugar free raspberry jello because that was in my pantry. Let that sit for 10 minutes then stirred in drained pineapple.
Layered other half of strawberries in quarters over parchment lined 9x13 inch pan. Poured pineapple, strawberry, jello mixture on top of the strawberries. Poured mixed cake mix following box directions with my addition and substitution, over that topping. 
Baked 15 minutes more after the center of cake rises. It was perfect. We ate the first piece warm. No marshmallows used. I forgot the whipped cream. Still good. Topping was of smooth glaze consistency, not thick, not rubbery not grainy as others stated. Will bake again using peaches,cloves, and cinnamon.

I made a few adjustments to this recipe based on other reviews. I quartered the strawberries, sprinkled with brown sugar and allowed them to macerate before smashing them with a potato masher. I made a bundt cake and it turned out beautifully. After placing the prepared strawberries into a greased bundt pan, I only used 3oz of jello (sprinkle). This allowed the juices to run down the sides of the bundt cake after it was inverted. Using more jello would have thickened the strawberries too much. This is not a sweet cake, but for my family's tastes, it was delicious and so quick to prepare.

Made this twice as-is in a springform pan (placed on a baking sheet to catch the juices) instead of 9x13...everyone loved it. Tried it today with diced fresh South Carolina peaches and peach Jell-o instead...wow!!!

This recipe is super easy to make and comes out delicious! It's not a super sweet cake which we love because it allows the sweetness of the strawberries to be the focus point. I was pleasantly surprised at the way the marshmallows melted and rose to the top of the cake and still didn't overpower in any way with their sweetness. I used sugar-free jello and it worked perfectly and lent an extra zing of bright red color to the already ripe strawberries. I also added a dash of strawberry extract to the cake batter thinking it would add another layer of strawberry taste, but honestly it was barely detectable, so I won't bother doing that again. Also flipping a cake from a 9 x 13 pan, while doable, can be a bit daunting, so next time I'll use multiple smaller pans. This will make flipping and storing easier. This recipe could be used for any kind of seasonal fresh fruit - just imagine using apples and cinnamon, pears with ginger or cardamon, peaches, berries - you can let your imagination go wild with this recipe. Thanks for sharing this one!

I have made this several times for family and friends and it disappears quickly. It is decadent served hot from the oven with a scoop of vanilla ice cream next to it, or chill it in the refrigerator overnight and serve it with whipped cream on top, cold. I chop/mash at least 3 cups of strawberries sprinkled with sugar and it will defininately cover the bottom of a 9x13 cake pan (see photo). Be careful removing from oven gently and allow to cool and it will not fall and it will maintain it's height. I have used yellow cake and even strawberry cake mixes and either way it turns out moist and delicous.

I made this as written for the most part. I read a lot of the reviews and added extra strawberries. This is delicious. I took the advice of a reviewer and sprinkled sugar before mashing. This was a great suggestion. Next time I will put in a smaller pan, as I like my cake thicker. Other than that, I will make it again. Thank you for sharing this recipe!

Made this just now using almost exact ingredients. I did use only 3oz of Jello as others suggested. I decided to bake it per the time on the cake box vs the suggested time so as to not overbake. My total time was 29 minutes. It was moist & perfect. Very easy & yummy cake. Topped it with cool whip. Will make again for sure & likely mix up the fruit & jello just to experiment. I used a glass 9x13 sprayed with Pam. Came out very easily. Thx for such an easy, yummy cake.

This cake is awesome! I'm a diabetic so I used sugar free cake mix, sugar free jello, and sugar free whipped topping. The only "sugar" ingredient was the marshmallows. It came out great! I used a bundt pan and I love the look of the cake after taking out of the pan. I've made this several times already and everyone enjoys it.

Only change that I made is to use a 3 oz package of Jello. Also the cake mix is now a smaller package but that seemed to be fine. I made a mistake and used a larger pan and so the cake was thinner and more like a bar cookie. HOWEVER the flavor was wonderful and I will make it again and in the correct size pan.
I ended up not doing enough strawberries, so next time I will try frozen thawed strawberries since you crush them anyways. It was really good otherwise.
This was so good! We had it tonight and wow everyone loved it. We had it with whipped cream but I think it might be better with ice cream🥹
Easy to make! Used Sugar free Strawberry Jello and Pillsbury Gluten Free 17 oz. yellow cake mix, it was great! Bit fallen in the middle but still tasted special! I served it with vanilla ice cream.

This came out great! I used Krusteaz gluten free cake mix. It didn't rise a ton, but it worked well and tasted delicious. I saw another comment about their coming out more like a bar than a cake. That's what I got. I don't know what mix they used. That said, I have another one in the oven right now because we loved it so much.
this is a really delicious cake. I don't make any changes to it
I have been making this delicious cake for years, this is by far the best recipe.
The very best strawberry dessert.. Very tasty & simple to make.
